# test_validate_password.py
import pytest

from your_module import validate_password  # replace with the actual module name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "password",
    [
        "Abcdefg1",       # exactly 8 chars
        "Password1",      # typical valid password
        "A1bcdef!",       # includes special character
        "ABCdef123",      # multiple uppercase/lowercase/digits
        "Äbcdefg1",       # unicode uppercase character
    ],
)
def test_validate_password_valid_passwords(password):
    assert validate_password(password) is True


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "password",
    [
        "",               # empty
        "Ab1",            # too short, despite meeting char requirements
        "Abcdef1",        # 7 chars
        "abcdefg1",       # missing uppercase
        "ABCDEFG1",       # missing lowercase
        "Abcdefgh",       # missing digit
        "12345678",       # missing upper and lower
        "!!!!!!!!",       # missing upper, lower, and digit
        "ABCdefgh",       # missing digit
        "abc12345",       # missing uppercase
        "ABC12345",       # missing lowercase
    ],
)
def test_validate_password_invalid_passwords(password):
    assert validate_password(password) is False


def test_validate_password_minimum_length_boundary():
    assert validate_password("Abcdef1") is False  # 7 chars
    assert validate_password("Abcdefg1") is True  # 8 chars


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "invalid_input",
    [
        None,
        12345678,
    ],
)
def test_validate_password_invalid_input_type_raises_type_error(invalid_input):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        validate_password(invalid_input)


def test_validate_password_bytes_input_raises_attribute_error_when_long_enough():
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        validate_password(b"Abcdefg1")
